message.reasoning_content:
Bugfix

The previous solution did a very expensive DCN-V2 model with 5-fold CV and a very short patience, but the budget (300s) was far exceeded. The training script overran the time limit. I need a simpler, fast training.

This is a tabular dataset with ~8k rows and 21 categorical features. A gradient boosting model (HistGradientBoosting or similar) will train in a fraction of a second and do just as well or better than the DCN-V2 approach on this data.

The plan: replace the torch model training with a scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier, using ordinal-encoded categorical features and one-hot / target encodings. To stay safe with categorical data, use ordinal encoding with ordinal-coded categorical columns and let HGB handle it via `categorical_features` indices. This is much faster than 5-fold DCN training.

We preserve the FeatureBuilder pipeline, the CLI, the thresholding logic, and the artifact persistence. We keep the OOF fold loop but use HistGradientBoosting (much cheaper). Optionally we could use a single model rather than 5 folds if time is tight.
